acceptance_criteria: PlanVerdict.cost_estimate's declared type and validators are quoted before any change.
A recoverable numeric string coerces to the declared type and the coercion is counted, demonstrated by a test.
A non-recoverable string is still rejected, demonstrated.
An exact number is unaffected, demonstrated.
Ruling D26 appears verbatim and B27 is closed or left open with the reason.
Other numeric verdict fields are listed and the ruling's reach is stated explicitly.
No type relaxed to Any — asserted.
Suite count reported before and after.
assumptions: The rejection is a Pydantic validator on the verdict model, and the same counting mechanism used elsewhere in the repo can be reused rather than built.
constraints: RULED BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (Ruling D26, issued in this command). Record the ruling before implementing it: a numeric verdict field coerces a string when the number is unambiguously recoverable, and the coercion is counted. If no number is recoverable, the rejection stands.

FIRST, VERIFY THE PREMISE: locate PlanVerdict.cost_estimate and quote its declared type and its validator. Confirm float_parsing is the rejection path. If the field is already coercing, the premise is wrong — say so and return NO_ACTION.

THE RULING'S TEST IS RECOVERABILITY, not shape: '$989.88 per month' recovers 989.88 and coerces; 'approximately one thousand' does not and is rejected. A coercion must never invent a number the text does not carry.
COUNT EVERY COERCION, per convention 21 and the -011 precedent: the normalization is ruled, counting it is repair. A coercion that hides how often it fires cannot be withdrawn later on evidence.
Do NOT apply this to a field where the number is not the field's subject. If a field is genuinely free text, this ruling does not reach it — say so rather than coercing.
Do NOT relax a type to Any. Coerce to the declared type or reject; never accept the string itself.

One test per class, each simulating its condition end to end (convention 22): a recoverable string coerces and is counted; a non-recoverable string is rejected and counted; an exact number is unaffected; and a wrong-typed non-string (a list, an object) is still rejected.
Prove the coercion test by breaking it: remove the coercion and show the rejection return, then restore and show the count.
Report whether the same class exists on other numeric verdict fields, by reading the models. If it does, name them and say whether the ruling reaches them — do not silently extend it.
Keep the diff small. Suite reported before and after.

objective: Decide and implement whether a numeric verdict field must coerce an information-preserving string, closing B27 — the schema rejection that discarded a recoverable plan cost.

preconditions.expected: Present. If absent, return BLOCKED naming ARCH-20260925-065.
Locate the field and its declared type; record it.
Locate the existing normalization and counting mechanism to reuse.

questions: Does shape-selects-the-test generalise to verdict fields, as the executor asked? My reading: only partially — a verdict field has one declared type, so the question is recoverability, not shape. State whether the code agrees.
Is the plan cost estimate consumed anywhere that a coerced float would change a decision? If it is, the coercion touches a conclusion and belongs in its own ruling rather than here.
rollback: Revert the commit; the field returns to rejecting an information-preserving string.
transport: Commit this command file verbatim as carriage before executing; commit the response IN_PROGRESS first, then update it in place. delivery_state must carry the PR number per Ruling D16.
